title: When the Summer Burns
premise: Rosalind Quintana inherited her family's failing vineyard along with a mountain of debt, and she has one winter to produce a salvageable vintage before the bank takes everything. When a freak snowstorm traps her with Jonah Reyes—the rival winemaker who was once the best mistake of her twenties—old wounds and older desires resurface faster than either can ration them. As Rosalind's found family of misfit vineyard workers rallies around her, she must choose between a safe marriage of convenience that would save the land and the reckless, wholehearted love she swore never to risk again. In the end, she bets the entire vineyard—and her entire heart—on a joint venture with Jonah, discovering that duty kept alive only what love could make worth keeping.
about_author: Quentin Iversen is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent a decade working harvests across the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction. He writes love stories set in working landscapes, where romance and labor are inseparable.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She walks the frost-bitten rows of Quintana Vineyard, tallying debts her father left hidden in a shoebox of receipts. Her crew of misfits—Marisol, Dev, and old Tomás—insist the harvest can be saved. Beat: grim determination masking grief; she vows the heart is a muscle she can train to stay quiet.

chapters.title: The Banker's Smile
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The bank gives her until spring: produce a viable vintage or lose the land. A neighboring vintner offers a rescue—marriage to his son, merging properties. Beat: humiliation and cold pragmatism; duty begins its campaign against desire.

chapters.title: Jonah Reyes, of All People
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At a regional growers' auction, she collides with Jonah, her winemaking rival and the man she loved and left a decade ago. Their bidding war over a barrel of yeast turns personal. Beat: sparks sharpened into armor; old history crackling under professional contempt.

chapters.title: The Crew Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The vineyard's ragtag staff debates staying through a brutal winter without pay they may never see. Marisol argues Rosalind is family, not employer. Beat: warmth and loyalty; the found family takes root, and Rosalind overhears, undone by being believed in.

chapters.title: A Storm with Good Timing
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A freak early snowstorm strands Rosalind and Jonah together at the vineyard after a failed negotiation over sharing equipment. Roads close; the power flickers. Beat: forced proximity, mutual resentment curdling into uneasy truce over candlelight and bad wine.

chapters.title: What We Did at Twenty-Four
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Snowbound, Jonah remembers the summer they made wine together and made love badly, before Rosalind vanished to protect her father's reputation. He confronts her; she deflects with arithmetic. Beat: confession meets deflection; the past stops being deniable.

chapters.title: The First Honest Hour
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. With the generator dead, they share one honest hour by the fireplace—apologies without excuses. Jonah admits he never stopped choosing her; she admits she never stopped running. Beat: tenderness breaking through, immediately resealed; a kiss that both regret and don't.

chapters.title: Thaw and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The roads open; Jonah leaves before dawn, leaving a note and a proposal: co-ferment their fruit into one wine, split everything. Rosalind reads it twice and files it under 'impossible.' Beat: hope offered and shelved; pride reasserting itself.

chapters.title: The Convenient Groom
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The neighbor's son, Elliott, is kind, sensible, and offers to clear her debt outright. Her crew watches her weigh the proposal like a contract clause. Beat: suffocating reasonableness; the reader sees the trap she can't.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Winter work begins in earnest; the crew teaches Rosalind that pruning is choosing what to cut so the vine can live. She quietly starts the co-fermentation experiments in a locked barn. Beat: metaphor made muscle; secret hope taking root alongside the vines.

chapters.title: Cellar Visits
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah arrives weekly under equipment pretenses to check the secret barrels. Their collaboration becomes flirtation becomes ritual. Beat: joy sneaking in sideways; both pretending this is only about wine.

chapters.title: The Taste of Maybe
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The experimental blend is startlingly good—better than either vineyard's solo effort. For one evening they celebrate like kids, dancing in the cellar. Beat: peak sweetness before the fall; Rosalind almost says the whole word 'love.'

chapters.title: Elliott Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Elliott discovers the joint barrels and the cellar dance's aftermath. He isn't cruel—he simply withdraws the offer, noting Rosalind can't marry a man while fermenting a future with another. Beat: consequences arrive without villains; duty's price comes due.

chapters.title: The Note in the Shoebox
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol finds a letter in the debt shoebox: Rosalind's father knew the vineyard was failing and begged her not to sacrifice her life to it. She gives it to Rosalind. Beat: posthumous absolution; the found family forcing the truth into the light.

chapters.title: Running Math
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind runs the numbers a hundred ways; the co-venture can't close before the bank deadline without Jonah's name on her debt, which means his vineyard collateral too. She refuses to gamble his livelihood. Beat: love against duty inverted—she pushes him away to protect him, repeating her oldest wound.

chapters.title: The Fight in the Cold
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah storms the vineyard, furious at being protected without consent. They fight in the frost, saying the unforgivable true things: she left him once to be noble, and she's doing it again. Beat: climax of conflict; both hearts fully exposed and bleeding.

chapters.title: The Bank Comes Early
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The bank moves up the deadline. Rosalind prepares to sign the vineyard away rather than ask Jonah for anything. The crew refuses to help her pack, standing in the doorway like a wall. Beat: rock bottom; the found family becomes her spine when hers gives out.

chapters.title: One Barrel, One Bet
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah presents the secret blend blind to a prestigious judging panel, wagering his own vineyard's collateral on its medal. Rosalind learns what he's risked only after the fact. Beat: he answers her sacrifice with his own; love demonstrated, not declared.

chapters.title: Gold, or Nothing
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Judgment day. The wine takes a silver—one rank short of the prize that saves them both. Rosalind, for the first time, chooses feeling over arithmetic: she tells Jonah the truth in front of everyone. Beat: climax; she bets the whole heart, win or lose.

chapters.title: What the Silver Bought
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The silver medal, plus the buzz it generates, brings an investor offer—but only for a partnership, not a rescue. The crews of both vineyards vote to merge as equals. Beat: found family expands into found enterprise; duty and love finally aligned.

chapters.title: First Frost, Last Debt
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. One year later: the merged Quintana-Reyes crush begins. Rosalind and Jonah marry nobody and each other, signing papers with ink-stained hands. Beat: resolution and release; the heart, she admits, was never containable, only waiting.

chapters.title: The Best Vintage
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue. At the harvest festival, the crew toasts the wine made from the storm-stranded winter. Rosalind names the blend 'When the Summer Burns' and finally believes she deserves what stayed. Beat: quiet joy; identity rebuilt not around duty, but around being loved.
